title: XOR.DDoS_Incident_Response_Scenario_512
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise by the XOR.DDoS malware family, specifically the Groundhog backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected unusual network activity on its Linux servers. Initial analysis suggests a potential compromise by the XOR.DDoS malware family, specifically the Groundhog backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target server with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target server's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. Enter `start` to begin the scenario.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. You have SSH access to the target server with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target server's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. Enter `start` to begin the scenario.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: You have noticed unusual outbound network connections from the target server. Investigate these connections to identify any suspicious activity. Submit the port number used for the suspicious connection.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and recent logs for any unusual patterns. The suspicious port is 4444 and the destination IP address is 192.168.50.5.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and recent logs for any unusual patterns.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for connections to port 4444 and the IP address 192.168.50.5.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious activity is maintained across reboots. Identify the persistence mechanism used by the malware. Submit the systemd service unit file name associated with the suspicious activity.
levels.solution: Look for systemd services or cron jobs that might be related to the suspicious activity. The systemd service unit file associated with the suspicious activity is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd services or cron jobs that might be related to the suspicious activity.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd service unit files for any suspicious services.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Check for any evidence of lateral movement from the target server to other hosts in the network. Submit the service name responsible for lateral movement.
levels.solution: Examine logs and system configurations for any signs of remote access or file transfers. The service responsible for lateral movement is `payload-transfer.service` and the destination host is `next-target`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine logs and system configurations for any signs of remote access or file transfers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that transfer files to other hosts.
